proposition: Let a_0 = 2, a_1 = 5 and a_n = 5*a_(n-1) + (-6)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 20, a_n = 1*2^n + 1*3^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: At n = 0 the closed form gives 2, matching a_0 = 2.
At n = 1 the closed form gives 5, matching a_1 = 5.
The closed form satisfies the recurrence: for every n in [0, 18], f(n+2) = 5*f(n+1) + (-6)*f(n).
There exists an integer n in [1, 20] with n^2 > 20.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 20].
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 20 we have n^2 >= 2n.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
Every integer n in [1, 20] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
Two base cases plus the recurrence identity give the closed form for every n in [0, 20].
